title: Sliced flank steak
skill: Trimming and slicing against the grain

notes.text: For more than 4, sear the steaks one at a time so the pan stays hot, and roast the potatoes on two sheet pans.

move.title: Trim, sear, rest, slice
move.body: Flank steak is lean, full of flavor, and tough if it's cut wrong. You'll trim off its silverskin, sear it hard, rest it, and slice it thin across the grain, the way a steakhouse does, with a parsley and garlic sauce and roasted potatoes.

why.title: Silverskin doesn't melt
why.body: The thin, shiny membrane on the surface of a flank steak tightens and turns rubbery in the pan. Slide the knife tip under it, angle the blade up, and pull it away in strips.

why.title: Dry, then hot
why.body: Pat the steak completely dry and get the pan smoking before it goes in. Surface water has to boil off before browning can start; a dry steak in a hot pan browns in minutes.

why.title: Rest before slicing
why.body: Hot meat's juices are under pressure. Ten minutes on the board lets them settle back into the fibers, so they stay in the slices instead of running across the board.

why.title: Across the grain, on an angle
why.body: Flank's long fibers run the length of the steak. Slicing across them, ¼ inch thick, on a 45° angle, cuts each fiber short, so every slice is tender.

why.title: Whole cuts at 145°F
why.body: The app's standard for a whole cut of beef is 145°F, which is medium. A seared whole cut is a smaller risk than ground meat, since its inside was never exposed, but this app still asks for 145°F.

wrong.fix: They were cut along the grain. Turn the steak 90° and cut the rest across the lines.

wrong.sign: The outside is gray, not brown
wrong.fix: The pan wasn't hot enough or the steak was wet. Dry the next one well and wait for the oil to smoke.

wrong.sign: A pool of juice on the board
wrong.fix: It wasn't rested long enough. Spoon the juice over the slices.
Let it sit 10 minutes; the garlic mellows in the lemon and oil.

choices: A thin membrane that turns rubbery in the pan
It cuts the long fibers short, so each slice is tender
quiz.explain: Along the grain, slices are stringy.

choices: Lets the juices settle so they stay in the meat
quiz.explain: Slice it right away and the juice runs out.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the middle.
Halve the potatoes, toss them on the sheet pan with the potatoes' oil and salt, and roast cut side down until browned and tender.
Chop the parsley fine and mince the garlic. Stir them in the small bowl with the lemon's zest and juice, the chili flakes, the sauce's oil, and salt.
Pat the steak dry. Trim off any fat and all the silverskin, then season both sides with the steak's salt and pepper.
steps.look: A dull, red surface with no shiny patches.

steps.text: Throw the paper towels away. Wash your hands, the knife, and the board with hot, soapy water.
Heat the oil in the skillet over high heat until it just smokes. Lay the steak in with the tongs, away from you.
Wash the tongs and your hands.
Sear without moving until a dark crust forms, then turn and sear the other side.
steps.look: A deep brown crust on both sides.

steps.text: Check the thickest part from the side: at least 145°F. If not, turn and cook 1 minute more.
Move the steak to the clean board and rest it.
Find the grain. Slice across it, ¼ inch thick, with the knife at a 45° angle.
steps.look: Short fibers on each slice's cut face.

steps.text: Fan the slices on a platter with the potatoes, and spoon the herb sauce over.
